description:
FOUND s488 (Fable, 2026-09-17) answering the USER's question "when the installed Perl is updated, must we reinstall PCL? should the Perl version go into the cache file names?".

WHAT THE KEYS HOLD TODAY (read from the code):
  * module entry name = sxhash(abs path | *pcl-cache-generation* | "v2" | p-compiler-stamp); the fasl adds *pcl-runtime-identity* (runtime source + SBCL).
  * p-compiler-stamp (`%p-compute-compiler-stamp`, #1119) = the compiler ROOT path + mtime:size of every Pl/**.pm one level deep + pl2cl.  NOTHING about the perl that runs pl2cl, and nothing about PPI.
  * eval entry stem (`%p-eval-cache-stem`) = generation + package + features + captures + text.  Same gap.
  * the transpiler's PROTO memo (`Pl::ProtoCache::_key`) DOES carry `$PPI::VERSION` and `$]` -- so the compile-time FACTS are safe, the cached EMISSION is not.
  * validity (p-cache-valid-p) = cache newer than the source's mtime + the .deps manifest's content hashes; neither sees the tokenizer.

WHY IT MATTERS: the emission is a function of PPI's token stream (PCL's repairs are keyed on 1.291's; a PPI point release that fixes one of docs/ppi-upstream-bugs.md changes the stream for the affected shapes).  Upgrade PPI in place -> the same module path, the same content, the same PCL files -> every cached .lisp stays VALID and runs on the OLD tokenizer's parse.  A perl upgrade usually moves the library dirs (5.38 -> 5.40), so module PATHS change and the keys with them -- the hole is the in-place case: a same-version perl rebuild, a distro PPI update, `cpanm PPI`.

NOT a reinstall question: nothing about perl is baked into the installed tree or the core (bin wrappers exec the real script; `pcl` runs the `perl` on PATH; /home/bernt/perl5/perlbrew/perls/perl-5.40.3/lib/site_perl/5.40.3/x86_64-linux /home/bernt/perl5/perlbrew/perls/perl-5.40.3/lib/site_perl/5.40.3 /home/bernt/perl5/perlbrew/perls/perl-5.40.3/lib/5.40.3/x86_64-linux /home/bernt/perl5/perlbrew/perls/perl-5.40.3/lib/5.40.3 is emitted per run from that perl).  After a perl upgrade only PPI >= 1.291 and Moo must exist FOR THE NEW PERL (the installer's `module_version` check uses $^X at install time only) -- a missing PPI fails loudly ("Can't locate PPI.pm"), so that half is not silent.

FIX SHAPE (mtime+size, NOT a version string -- the stamp's own discipline, and a rebuilt same-version perl or a patched PPI would fool a version string): extend `%p-compiler-files` with (a) the perl BINARY `pcl` will spawn (resolve `perl` on PATH once per process; truename + stat) and (b) PPI's files (locate `PPI.pm` through the preamble's `*p-core-inc-dirs*` / the runtime's /home/bernt/perl5/perlbrew/perls/perl-5.40.3/lib/site_perl/5.40.3/x86_64-linux /home/bernt/perl5/perlbrew/perls/perl-5.40.3/lib/site_perl/5.40.3 /home/bernt/perl5/perlbrew/perls/perl-5.40.3/lib/5.40.3/x86_64-linux /home/bernt/perl5/perlbrew/perls/perl-5.40.3/lib/5.40.3, then walk `PPI/**/*.pm` like the Pl/ walk; ~100 stats, well under 1 ms).  The perl-side twin `Pl::ProtoCache::_compiler_stamp` gets the same two inputs so the two stamps keep agreeing (rule 11: they are documented as the SAME set).  Fold the same stamp into `%p-eval-cache-stem`.  Cost on a warm run: the stats; measure with `pcl -e 1` best-of-5 before/after.

GUARD: Pl/t/module-fasl-cache-01.t rows -- (1) touch a fake `PPI/Token.pm` on a private PERL5LIB dir -> the next run MISSES (new key); (2) a perl binary swap simulated by PATH -> a different key; (3) an untouched tree -> the same key twice (the memo must stay stable).  Docs: docs/caching.md Â§2 "what invalidates" gains the two inputs; docs/ir-spec.md Â§9.2b's key line.  One filler; no emission change.
=== DONE (s488b) ===

The compiler fingerprint now hashes, on BOTH sides (the runtime's
`%p-compute-compiler-stamp` and `Pl::ProtoCache::_compiler_stamp` -- they are
documented as the SAME set, rule 11):

  * THE PERL BINARY `pcl` will spawn -- `perl` as resolved on `$PATH` once per
    process, by truename + mtime + size.  A VERSION STRING was rejected as the
    fix, and that is the finding: a rebuilt same-version perl, or a perlbrew
    switch between two 5.40.3 builds, has the same `$]` and a different
    tokenizer.
  * PPI's SOURCES -- `PPI.pm` located through `*p-core-inc-dirs*` (runtime
    side) / `@INC` (perl side), then `PPI/**/*.pm` walked exactly as the `Pl/`
    walk walks PCL's own files.  95 files here.

The same stamp is folded into `%p-eval-cache-stem`, so the string-eval cache
moves with it, and `pcl --cache-info` asks through a real preamble and names
both inputs (the perl binary's path and the PPI file count).

MEASURED COST (`pcl -e 1`, best-of-5, warm core): the stamp itself 1.15 ms ->
1.95 ms per process, i.e. ~95 extra stat(2)s.  Invisible in a run's wall time
(a one-line script is 0.165 s end to end).

GUARDS, `Pl/t/module-fasl-cache-01.t` 59 -> 65 rows: a touched fake
`PPI/Token.pm` on a private PERL5LIB dir gives a NEW key; a wrapper `perl`
earlier on `$PATH` (which execs the real one from another directory) gives a
DIFFERENT key; an untouched tree gives the SAME key twice (the per-process
memo stays stable).  `Pl/t/cache-surface-01.t` gained the `--cache-info` rows.

Docs: `docs/caching.md` Â§2 ("what invalidates an entry") + Â§5's cost table,
`docs/ir-spec.md` Â§9.2b's key line.  corpus-diff IDENTICAL over 111 (no
emission change, no generation bump).

Related: #1861 (the emission-selecting environment joined the same stamp in
this batch), #1841 (the script cache, which this had to land before).
subject: DONE s488b: the module-cache and eval-cache KEYS fingerprinted PCL's OWN compiler files only, so a PPI upgrade or a perl rebuild (same paths, different tokenizer) left every cached transpile VALID -- the stamp now hashes the perl binary on $PATH (truename+mtime+size) and all 95 PPI/**/*.pm on BOTH sides, folded into %p-eval-cache-stem; measured cost 1.15 -> 1.95 ms per process
